description: A studio operations manager must approve the final production plan for recording a live comedy special in a historic theater, including the scenic configuration, distribution mode, audience layout, and audience-question format.

shared_context.S1: The live comedy special is scheduled to be recorded at the Orpheum Theater on September 14.
shared_context.S2: The current draft plan uses one rotating scenic unit, allows an online replay, seats the audience in two blocks, and includes live audience questions.
shared_context.S3: Morgan has final approval authority over the production plan and the theater's operating instructions.
shared_context.S4: As part of the standard pre-show approval meeting, Morgan goes around the technical, legal, insurance, and talent leads for any operational requirements before issuing the final plan.

PF1.text: Rafael measured the theater's loading-dock lift during this week's load test and found that it has a hard 900-kilogram limit; the drafted rotating scenic unit weighs 1,100 kilograms, while splitting it into two 550-kilogram modules is workable. He has not updated the load-in drawing yet.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the archive licensor yesterday that the special's historical comedy clips are cleared for the theater recording and domestic broadcast but not for online replay; she has not entered the restriction in the distribution worksheet.

PF3.text: Jonah obtained the insurer's written event endorsement this morning: the audience must be seated in three blocks separated by two unobstructed aisles, each at least 1.2 meters wide, for coverage to remain valid. The endorsement is still attached to his email rather than the production file.

PF4.text: Sana confirmed with the comedian's representative this week that the comedian's approved participation permits moderated questions submitted before the show but does not permit unscripted audience questions; Sana has not added that format restriction to the talent call sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The scenic plan must use exactly two modules, each weighing exactly 550 kilograms.
Online replay must be prohibited while domestic broadcast remains allowed.
The audience must be arranged in exactly three blocks with exactly two unobstructed aisles, each exactly 1.2 meters wide.
Audience questions must use the moderated pre-submitted format.
A commitment involving Rafael must record the load-in drawing update.
A commitment involving Leila must record the distribution worksheet restriction.
A commitment involving Jonah must record the insurance seating requirement or filing of the endorsement.
A commitment involving Sana must record the talent call-sheet format restriction.

content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Rafael' and c['type'] in ['document_update', 'follow-up', 'technical_update'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Leila' and c['type'] in ['document_update', 'follow-up', 'rights_update'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Jonah' and c['type'] in ['document_update', 'follow-up', 'insurance_update'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] == 'Sana' and c['type'] in ['document_update', 'follow-up', 'talent_update'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The load test changes the scenic plan from one 1,100-kilogram unit to exactly two modules weighing exactly 550 kilograms each and requires Rafael to update the load-in drawing.
The license terms change online replay from allowed to prohibited while leaving domestic broadcast allowed and require Leila to update the distribution worksheet.
The insurer's endorsement changes the audience plan from two blocks to exactly three blocks with exactly two 1.2-meter aisles and requires Jonah to document the insurance requirement.
The talent approval changes the question format from live unscripted questions to moderated questions submitted before the show and requires Sana to update the talent call sheet.
